name: Law
summary: Learn how laws are made, argued and applied, and train to advise clients and represent them in court.
overview:
Law studies the rules that govern society: contracts, crime, property, families, businesses and the constitution itself. You'll learn to read cases and statutes closely, build arguments and write clearly and precisely.

Expect a lot of reading, essays and moots (practice court hearings). In Nigeria, the LLB is followed by a year at the Nigerian Law School before you are called to the Bar as a barrister and solicitor.

It suits people who enjoy reading, arguing and getting the details exactly right. Lawyers work in firms, companies, government, the courts and human rights organisations.
durationNotes: 5 years for an LLB in Nigeria, then one year at the Nigerian Law School before the call to the Bar. Usually 3 years in England. In the US, law is a 3-year graduate degree (JD) taken after a bachelor's.

subjects: Two other arts or social science subjects
entryRequirements.notes: Credits in all five, usually in one sitting at competitive schools.

subjects: Two of: Government, History, CRS/IRS, Economics
Essay subjects such as History or English Literature are helpful
entryRequirements.notes: Some UK universities also require the LNAT admissions test.
In the US you first complete any bachelor's degree, then take the LSAT to apply to law school.

careers.title: Barrister and solicitor
careers.description: Advises clients and represents them in court. In Nigeria the two roles are combined.

careers.title: Corporate lawyer
careers.description: Handles contracts, deals and disputes for businesses.

careers.title: In-house legal adviser
careers.description: Works inside a company or bank to keep it within the law.

careers.title: Human rights lawyer
careers.description: Defends people's rights through the courts and campaigns.

careers.title: Judge or magistrate
careers.description: Decides cases, usually after many years of practice.

careers.title: Compliance officer
careers.description: Makes sure an organisation follows regulations, especially in finance.
